program: Wingless raw-input to invariant representation to reasoning chain
question: Can the current exact raw motifs be converted into surface-invariant canonical representations using only data-derived distributional signatures, restoring cross-family reasoning without an evaluator alias dictionary?
hypothesis: If each recurrent surface motif is assigned a raw occurrence-count signature from a frozen calibration corpus, the two aliases of each of four values and five operations will form nine unique equal-signature pairs. Canonicalizing each pair before transition learning will restore at least 0.95 cross-family semantic accuracy while an otherwise identical unbridged surface learner remains at or below 0.25.

portfolio_context.reason: directly repair the alias-invariance failure exposed by the preceding substrate falsification

prior_evidence.observation: Same-family semantic accuracy was 1.0, cross-family accuracy was 0.0625, and all 160 cross-family transition keys were absent.

scope_statement: This is a bounded distributional canonicalization mechanism. Passing shows that surface aliases can be merged from frozen occurrence statistics; it does not establish general semantic equivalence learning.
authority: research-only; no deployment, external-model inference, scheduler, queue, accepted-ref, production, broker, or live-interface authority

benchmark.transition_training: the same two independently complete alias families used by the falsification: all five operations on all sixteen value pairs, twenty repeats per family

calibration.construction: separate raw calibration records containing only one selected motif surrounded by deterministic high-byte noise; aliases of the same semantic item occur the same frozen number of times, and different semantic items use different counts
calibration.family_symmetry: both surface aliases of one semantic item receive the same signature count

representation_learner.input: raw transition-training plus raw calibration bytes
representation_learner.candidate: every contiguous four-byte window within record boundaries
representation_learner.selection: top eighteen transition-corpus recurrent motifs by occurrence count descending, then lexicographic raw key; calibration records are excluded from selection and used only after selection for signature measurement

alias_bridge.signature: exact count of each selected motif in the frozen calibration corpus
alias_bridge.pairing: within surface-value representations and within surface-operation representations, pair exactly two motifs only when their nonzero calibration signature is equal and unique to that pair
alias_bridge.canonical_id: sort alias pairs by signature count ascending and assign one canonical ID per pair
alias_bridge.forbidden: no evaluator semantic ID, family ID, motif-content lookup, operation semantics, or hand-written alias map may participate in pairing

learners.bridged: canonical operation ID plus canonical ordered value pair -> canonical output-pair counts
learners.unbridged_control: exact surface operation ID plus exact surface ordered value pair -> surface output-pair counts, identical to the falsified substrate
learners.prediction: argmax learned count distribution; evaluator semantics are used only after prediction for scoring

controls: Representation selection uses transition-training bytes only; calibration does not affect which motifs are selected.
Calibration pairing uses count equality only and cannot inspect evaluator semantic or family labels.
Both bridged and unbridged learners receive byte-for-byte identical decoded transition observations.
Same-family evaluation must remain strong for both learners.
Cross-family evaluation is identical to the preceding falsification.
No tokenizer, external model, network access, gradient optimizer, capacity growth, evaluator alias dictionary, oracle correction, or post-result tuning is permitted.
validity_criteria: Exact parent and North Star identities match.
Transition training is byte-for-byte the frozen two-family design from the preceding falsification except for experiment identity.
Calibration counts match the frozen value and operation signature lists exactly in both families.
Alias pairing uses only selected-representation type and equal nonzero calibration signature.
Each selected motif belongs to exactly one two-member signature group and no signature is shared by more than one semantic pair.
Both bridged and unbridged learners receive identical transition observations after their respective surface/canonical encoding.
All metrics are finite and full Go regression passes before the probe.
No evaluator semantic/family label influences alias pairing or prediction.

classification_rules.supported: All validity criteria and all twenty frozen thresholds pass.
classification_rules.mixed: Validity passes and bridged cross-family accuracy materially exceeds the unbridged control, but at least one pairing or 0.95 accuracy threshold fails.
classification_rules.negative: Validity passes but distributional canonicalization does not materially improve cross-family accuracy.
classification_rules.incomplete: Compute interruption prevents the full frozen matrix.
classification_rules.invalid: Any selection/calibration leakage, evaluator-label access, ambiguous pairing, deterministic-state, capacity, or qualification criterion fails.

stop_conditions: Stop invalid before scientific execution on parent, North Star, build, frozen-package, or calibration-construction drift.
After output begins, complete all pairing, same-family, and cross-family evaluations unless infrastructure prevents it.
Do not alter signature counts, add semantic cues, inspect evaluator labels during pairing, increase capacity, or weaken thresholds after observing output.
no_post_result_tuning_rule: No calibration signature, pairing rule, canonicalization, learner, evaluation, metric, threshold, or interpretation may change after any primary output is observed under this experiment identifier.
